dataset_identity.row_meaning: One individual sales transaction (purchase) made by a customer at a specific store on a given date
dataset_identity.time_behavior: Event log (each row is a timestamped transaction; dataset can be treated as panel if aggregated by customer)
health_observations: 20% missing values in Age may bias demographic analyses and segmentation.
10% missing values in Amount could affect revenue calculations; need imputation or exclusion strategies.
10% missing FeedbackScore limits reliability of satisfaction metrics; consider missing-not-at-random assessment.
Binary IsReturned has no missing values, enabling robust churn/return modeling.
Date field is string; ensure proper datetime conversion for time‑series aggregation.
misinterpretation_risks: Treating missing Age as random when it may correlate with privacy preferences or specific store locations.
Inferring causality from IsReturned to FeedbackScore without accounting for product category or amount spent.
Assuming each StoreLocation represents a distinct market segment without considering online orders that may share the same location label.
Using TransactionID as a predictive feature rather than as an identifier, leading to overfitting.
Aggregating across dates without adjusting for seasonality (e.g., holiday sales spikes).

user_intent.decision_supported: Predict likelihood of a transaction being returned to enable proactive customer service, inventory planning, and return‑prevention strategies
constraints: Impute or model missing Age carefully (possible bias)
Do not use TransactionID as a predictive feature
Convert Date to proper datetime and account for seasonality/holiday effects
Consider store location and online orders when defining market segments
Assess missingness in FeedbackScore and Amount before inclusion

modifications.impact: Missing ages bias demographic segmentation, age‑based lifetime value calculations, and any model using age as a predictor.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Impute missing Age with the median age computed within each (Gender, StoreLocation) group; if a group lacks sufficient data, fallback to overall median age.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Drop rows with missing Age (would lose 20% of records), global mean imputation (ignores demographic patterns), random value imputation (adds noise).
modifications.effect: All rows with Age null (≈20% of dataset) will receive an imputed numeric value; Age column type remains float64.

modifications.impact: Revenue aggregation, profit modeling, and price sensitivity analyses will be understated if missing amounts are ignored.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Impute missing Amount using the median transaction amount for the corresponding ProductCategory; if a category has no non‑missing values, use the overall median Amount.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Delete rows with missing Amount (lose 10% of data), global mean imputation (skews high‑value categories), predictive regression (adds model‑drift risk for a simple financial figure).
modifications.effect: All rows where Amount is null (≈10% of records) receive a category‑based median value; column remains float64.

modifications.impact: Customer satisfaction metrics and any downstream churn/return models that incorporate feedback will be biased if missingness is systematic.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Create a binary indicator IsFeedbackMissing, then impute missing FeedbackScore with a regression model (e.g., RandomForestRegressor) trained on Amount, ProductCategory, IsReturned, Age, and Gender. This acknowledges potential NOT‑AT‑RANDOM patterns while preserving predictive signal.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Simple median imputation (ignores relationship to other variables), dropping missing rows (loss of 10% data), treating missing as zero (misrepresents no feedback).
modifications.effect: Adds new column IsFeedbackMissing (bool). Imputed values replace nulls in FeedbackScore for ~10% of rows; datatype remains float64.

modifications.problem: Date column stored as object string without datetime conversion
modifications.impact: Time‑series aggregations, seasonal analysis, and lag feature engineering are impossible without proper datetime format.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Parse Date strings to pandas datetime (ISO‑8601 or known format), enforce UTC timezone, and create auxiliary columns Year, Month, Weekday for easier modeling.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Leave as string (prevents temporal analysis), manual manual parsing per row (error‑prone), dropping the column (loses essential temporal context).
modifications.effect: All rows (100%) have Date converted to datetime64[ns, UTC]; new integer columns Year, Month, Weekday added.

restricted_columns.TransactionID: primary identifier – must never be altered or used as a predictive feature
restricted_columns.Date: temporal anchor – must be kept and correctly typed
restricted_columns.IsReturned: binary outcome – no missing values, preserve original values

data_integrity.validation_result: Repaired dataset retains all original records, primary keys unchanged, timestamps correctly typed, and imputed numeric fields respect observed subgroup distributions, ensuring the reconstructed data faithfully represents the original transaction process.

anomalies: Amount distribution is right‑skewed; max $899 far exceeds median $120, indicating potential outlier purchases.
IsReturned is heavily imbalanced (8 of 10 transactions not returned), which may limit model performance.
Missing values: 20% Age, 10% Amount, 10% FeedbackScore – risk of missing‑not‑at‑random bias.
Date column stored as string; without datetime conversion, seasonal or trend analysis is unreliable.
Very small sample size (10 rows) limits statistical confidence and generalizability.

target_associations.Amount: Negatively correlated with Age (-0.28) and FeedbackScore (-0.33); higher spend tends to come from younger customers and is linked to slightly lower satisfaction scores.
target_associations.IsReturned: Imbalanced distribution (80% False) makes direct numeric correlation difficult; preliminary view suggests returns may concentrate in specific product categories or lower‑amount transactions, warranting deeper categorical analysis.
target_associations.FeedbackScore: Positive modest correlation with Age (0.20) and negative correlation with Amount (-0.33); older shoppers rate experiences slightly higher, while higher transaction values are associated with lower satisfaction.
